R0221.title: Cross-Virtual-Physical Identity Correlation Attack
R0221.definition: Attackers analyze users' behavior patterns and social relationships in the metaverse to reverse-track their real identity for targeted attacks or blackmail.

references.title: Analysis of identity-correlation attacks in the metaverse

R0221.description:
Cross-virtual-physical identity correlation attacks infer real identities or other platform accounts from virtual behavior, social graphs, device features, and transaction records. Attackers can then perform targeted scams, harassment, or extortion.

The risk comes from stitching together multiple low-sensitivity signals. Platforms should reduce identifier reuse and restrict exportable behavioral data.
R0221.influence: Identity correlation can deanonymize users across virtual and real contexts, enabling targeted scams, harassment, or extortion.

observables: User virtual behavior trails are correlated with off-chain identities and used for targeted extortion
Cross-scene behavior-identifier reuse causes virtual-identity deanonymization
Exportable behavior data is bulk-aggregated into highly sensitive profiles
Users' virtual-world social relationships are used to infer real-world identities
Deanonymization is followed by targeted scams or harassment against specific users
